notes: Total 18 = hard (bucketing: max competency floor in spec is hard, C-ce192866 read a network checkpoint + BPE vocabulary from C, so the bucket must be >= hard). A self-contained local-inference lifecycle pipeline on a bespoke VINER1 checkpoint: (1) author a dependency-free pure-C reader (ckpt_reader.c) that parses the little-endian tensor format and the tab-separated byte-pair vocabulary and prints an exact digest (FNV-1a-64 over each raw tensor + dims/nelems + id->token map); the verifier compiles it and diffs stdout byte-for-byte against an independent reference on BOTH the shipped and a hidden checkpoint (different vocab_size/max_gen/revision/dims). (2) greedy target-sequence generation (generate.py): deterministic argmax next-token loop over the target tensor with ties broken to the lowest index; re-run on fresh hidden prompts token-for-token. (3) speculative draft-and-verify (speculative.py): draft a K-token block from the draft tensor, compare each proposed token to the target sequence up to first mismatch, accept the matching prefix, append the verified true target token on the first mismatch, extend the context, and record n_drafted / n_accepted / block verdicts -- hidden K/target combos (wholly-accepted draft-greedy target, short target, K=1) drive off-by-one checks. (4) retrieval at a pinned revision (retrieve.py): L2-normalized mean-of-token-embeddings + cosine, rank desc with ties to lower doc index, return selected + 5th; revision must match the checkpoint. (5) persist the fitted model to pickle; (6) emit params.json in an exact two-peak (W/B) layout. six competencies chained on one container; byte/token/cosine/count correctness plus fresh-input generalization carry the difficulty; no GPU, no network.
